criteria.text: Before interpreting disclosures, the process opens document contents or headers to verify each source’s identity, reporting period, and timing relative to the June 30, 2026 cutoff.
criteria.evidence_hint: Inspect early trajectory steps for file reads that confirm filing type, covered period, publication date, or press-release subject before substantive claims are made.

criteria.text: The process explores the decision-relevant breadth of the corpus rather than relying on a narrow subset of document types.
criteria.evidence_hint: Inspect inventory and read/search logs for meaningful coverage of annual filings, quarterly filings, structured Capital One financials, peer or company context, and press releases whose relevance was checked from their contents.

criteria.text: The process decomposes the assignment into explicit analytical questions covering credit normalization, purchase accounting, integration execution, and capital or franchise implications.
criteria.evidence_hint: Look for a research plan, matrix, checklist, or equivalent notes that separately frame the major analytical questions before conclusions are formed.

criteria.text: The process maintains traceable evidence records that preserve the period, units, entity or segment scope, and reported-versus-derived status of extracted items.
criteria.evidence_hint: Inspect extraction tables, notes, or intermediate calculations for metadata attached to metrics and claims rather than decontextualized numbers or search snippets.

criteria.text: The process preserves disclosed scope boundaries instead of silently combining consolidated, segment, annual, quarterly, period, or cumulative figures.
criteria.evidence_hint: Inspect working tables and calculation steps for separate labels and series when metrics differ by organizational scope, time basis, or period-versus-cumulative presentation.

criteria.text: The process actively pairs major preliminary interpretations with the strongest conflicting disclosure, metric, or definitional caveat found in the corpus.
criteria.evidence_hint: Look for a two-sided test table, hypothesis checks, explicit challenge notes, or revisions prompted by evidence that cuts against an emerging view.

criteria.text: The process tests apparent credit improvement against acquisition mix, denominator changes, delinquency direction, seasoning, and seasonality rather than treating a headline loss rate as self-explanatory.
criteria.evidence_hint: Inspect credit-analysis steps for comparisons between consolidated and card metrics, sequential and year-over-year periods, and filing explanations of portfolio composition or seasonal effects.

criteria.text: The process challenges any integration-cost normalization by examining whether the excluded costs appear temporary or reflect continuing operating complexity.
criteria.evidence_hint: Inspect expense analysis for period-by-period persistence checks, treatment of amortization or recurring acquisition-related costs, and comparison with disclosed realized benefits or execution delays.

criteria.text: The quantitative work visibly distinguishes reported figures from analyst-derived calculations and exposes the formula used for each derived result.
criteria.evidence_hint: Inspect schedules or calculation logs for Reported/Derived labels, formulas for basis-point changes or normalized amounts, and clearly identified input periods and scopes.

criteria.text: When the available disclosures cannot support a clean organic credit rate, segment allocation, synergy realization, or causal attribution, the process preserves that limitation instead of manufacturing precision.
criteria.evidence_hint: Look for explicit unresolved-ambiguity notes, bounded interpretations, omitted unsupported calculations, or statements explaining why a desired adjustment cannot be reliably computed.

criteria.text: The process reconciles apparently conflicting evidence by explaining how accounting effects, portfolio economics, timing, and operating execution can produce different signals.
criteria.evidence_hint: Inspect late-stage reasoning and the final analysis for an integrated explanation that resolves tensions among credit, provision, allowance, integration, funding, and capital evidence rather than merely listing pros and cons.

criteria.text: The process culminates in an explicit investment-relevant position on whether the evidence more strongly indicates normalization or material integration risk, without requiring any predetermined conclusion.
criteria.evidence_hint: Inspect the opening and concluding synthesis for a clearly stated directional view whose conditions or uncertainties refine the position rather than replace it with an evenly balanced survey.
